findings.summary: WSL service denies ALL service RPCs from the validation shell (EnumerateDistros, CreateInstance -> E_ACCESSDENIED) despite WSL 2.7.10.0 installed, Ubuntu-22.04 registered (State=1), wslservice PID 7844 running, and a normal-looking token (Medium IL, INTERACTIVE present, no AppContainer). Prior closeout audit (2026-09-16, main@954514a) successfully ran WSL full suite + real stdio win->wsl from a harness session, so this is a new/transient service state. No user-level recovery attempted without approval; escalation to same sandbox mode rejected by policy.
findings.resolution: After the session's DSH file policy moved to danger-full-access (2026-09-18, user action), the identical wsl.exe command succeeded immediately: WSL_EXEC_OK, Ubuntu 22.04.5, kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2, user h00969597. Earlier denials were therefore caused by the prior restricted sandbox mode and/or transient WSL service state, not by a missing product capability. All WSL-dependent cells re-opened and proceeding.

findings.summary: G02 (same source compiled twice with -DMODE_VALUE=1 / -DMODE_VALUE=2): the per-context macro values ARE stored in the index DB (macros table: two rows, value '1' context 1d405fa4c07e76fc, value '2' context 9655faf2257c623d, def_source=command_line) but NO supported consumer surface exposes them. lookup_symbol('MODE_VALUE', exact=True) returns the FUNCTION mode_value rows via relaxed prefix fallback (_fallback: true); search_code never reaches macros_fts because function hits short-circuit the pipeline; explain_symbol('MODE_VALUE') returns 'Symbol not found'; fw-context export contains no macro/defines data; search_content shows only the unexpanded token in body text. Net effect: a consumer cannot tell which compile action carries which value — the distinguishing semantic of the two contexts is silently lost while both contexts exist as rows.
findings.secondary: macros.expanded_value is self-inconsistent for context 1d405fa4c07e76fc: value='1' but expanded_value='2' (clang -dM -E for -DMODE_VALUE=1 must expand to 1). Stored index data diverges from compiler truth (INDEX_DIVERGENCE evidence, same root cause area).

findings.summary: G04 (bare build + [[build.variants]] A/B/C, defines []/USE_USB=1/UNRELATED=1): the bare generator writes ONE shared compile_commands.json at cc_output_path(root) regardless of variant (src/fw_context_mcp/indexer/builders/manual.py:188-189). Per-variant artifacts are not isolated, so the last generated variant's defines win and every variant is indexed from identical flags. Observed: 3 distinct config_hashes recorded, but transport_send groups as ONE equivalence group [A,B,C] with identical body fingerprint; compare_variants(A,B) reports edges_equal=true although variant B compiles the #ifdef USE_USB branch (transport_send must call usb_send, not uart_send) — the tool asserts semantic equality of semantics that differ (WRONG_ANSWER surface). get_source(name, variant='B') additionally served the INACTIVE uart-branch body from disk (source_origin='disk', line 6) as if live, with no stale warning — for variant B the live body is line 3 (usb_send). Feature combination documented as supported (docs/configuration.md:60 'works for every build system, not only Zephyr'; docs:80 variant build_dir default 'build/<name>' not honored by the bare generator).

findings.summary: G07 (dead/keep): find_dead_code correctly classifies the mutually-recursive dead_a/dead_b as graph_unreachable with scc=[dead_a,dead_b] (L2) and correctly protects kept_by_linker (used attribute root evidence; never definite dead — linker oracle on WSL proves KEEP honors it: kept_by_linker is a T symbol in app.elf linked with --gc-sections -T linker.ld). The failure: main, live_root, live_leaf — a plainly live call chain (ENTRY main -> live_root -> live_leaf) — are ALL reported status=graph_unreachable ('called only by other unreachable code'). Root cause: the root set requires ENTRY() from a build-attested linker script; the manual/compile_commands backend never links and its get_linker_scripts returns [] by design (src/fw_context_mcp/indexer/builders/manual.py:237-243), linker.ld is absent from the files table (only main.c is recorded), memory_regions has 0 rows, and no configuration key exists to declare a linker script (grep for linker_script/ld_script across docs = no matches). Generic external linkage is deliberately not a root, so on any compile_commands-only project the tool structurally cannot root main and misreports the live entry chain as unreachable — a WRONG_ANSWER surfaced directly to consumers of the dead-code report. Not documented in KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md.
findings.secondary: Oracle nuance recorded honestly: clang 14 at -O0 already drops unreferenced static functions (dead_a/dead_b absent from main.o), so the final-image evidence covers the live chain + kept_by_linker; the product's dead_a/dead_b SCC classification itself matches source-level truth. The misclassification of the LIVE chain is independent of that nuance.

findings.summary: G10 (Cortex-M CMSIS vector table): get_vector_table correctly recognizes the 'vectors' array and names all 8 handler slots exactly (1=Reset_Handler, 2=NMI, 3=HardFault, 11=SVC, 14=PendSV, 15=SysTick, 16=IRQ0, 17=IRQ1) and correctly leaves reserved zero slots (4-10, 12, 13) unnamed. Slot 0 — the initial stack pointer (const pFunc vectors[] = { (pFunc)&__initial_sp, ... }) — is NOT resolved: coverage says 'No name in slots 0'. The underlying index HAS the evidence: symbols holds __initial_sp (varglobal) and refs holds the initializer reference (startup.c:13, ref_kind=ref), so the data-symbol slot is resolvable but the c-source table extraction only emits function-typed words. Consumers reading the table cannot see the initial-SP slot; the coverage note discloses the gap but not the recoverable name.
evidence: .fw-validation/artifacts/V1/G10/G10.result.json (slot_map_exact=false, initial_sp_is_data_slot0=false; 8 handler slots exact)
.fw-validation/artifacts/V1/G10/raw/responses.json (get_vector_table coverage: 'No name in slots 0, 4-10, 12-13')

findings.summary: Any function whose entire definition spans a single source line (end_line == line) stores symbols.source='' — its body is invisible to search_bodies and any body-semantic query. Cross-case DB evidence: G01 master_entry/slave_entry (1 line, srclen=0) vs feature_value/role_value (7 lines, stored); G03 helper (line 14-14, srclen=0) vs selected (lines 4-12, stored 44-80 chars); G12 active_line (1 line, srclen=0); G13 shared_value/f_000 (all single-line, srclen=0). get_source masks the symptom by falling back to disk (source_origin='disk'), but search_bodies — the documented definition-text surface — returns nothing for every one-liner function. This is the GENERAL root cause behind F-V1-002's narrower description: the G03 'helper' failure was an instance of single-line emptiness, not of conditional wrapping (G13 has no conditionals at all and shows the same emptiness). Consumers lose body-semantic search for a very common C style (one-line accessors/inlines). Classification: SILENT_DATA_LOSS (broadened trigger vs F-V1-002; G03 classification unchanged).
findings.amends: F-V1-002 (trigger analysis broadened; G03 verdict unchanged)

findings.summary: lookup_symbol/search_bodies/search_content cap results at limit<=100 (schema max) with no offset/page token, so a consumer cannot enumerate more than 100 same-name symbol rows in any single or composed query. G13 (n=250) needs 250 shared_value context rows; every query returns at most 100. The uncapped aggregate get_active_build.file_count==2n still evidences all 250 contexts, but per-row enumeration of >100 same-name symbols is impossible on the query surface. Impact: fanout audits and same-name symbol inventories at scale (>100) silently truncate.
evidence: artifacts/V1/G13/G13.result.json: rows_p=100 for n=100 and n=250 (cap), file_count 200/500 proves contexts exist
lookup_symbol schema: limit default 50 max 100; no offset parameter on any query tool
findings.repro: Generate 250 TUs sharing one header (G13 generate.py 250); lookup_symbol name=shared_value limit=100 -> exactly 100 rows; no parameter reaches the remaining 150.

findings.title: get_vector_table returns false 'No vector table' for the standard CMSIS 6 startup template C table
findings.expected: vector table recognized: __VECTOR_TABLE[240] with slot0=__INITIAL_SP, Reset_Handler, NMI/HardFault/... , Interrupt0-9, zero-filled tail (oracle dump artifacts/V2/C1/startup_vector_region.txt)
observed: get_vector_table -> 'No vector table in this build... no array of function addresses was recognised'
the table IS indexed as a symbol: lookup __VECTOR_TABLE (exact) -> varglobal startup_ARMCM3.c:80
element type collapsed: signature 'const int[240]' (typedef'd function-pointer VECTOR_TABLE_Type lost)
search_bodies on the array initializer -> empty (F-V1-007 class: stored body empty)
find_references __INITIAL_SP -> 'Symbol not found' (slot-0 data symbol unresolved, F-V1-006 class)
findings.analysis: conditional branches evaluate correctly (ARMCM3 if=1, __GNUC__ if=1) — the table region IS in the active view; the vector-table shape recognizer rejects the standard CMSIS 6 template form: typedef'd function-pointer element type + cast first element ((VECTOR_TABLE_Type)(&__INITIAL_SP)) + integer-0 reserved slots + __VECTOR_TABLE_ATTRIBUTE macro. The false 'no table' claim is a WRONG_ANSWER (presence claimed absent), not merely a silent omission. CONTRAST (Z4): on the same product build (qemu_cortex_m3, zephyr), the ASSEMBLY vector table is fully recognized (97 slots: SP data slot, z_arm_reset, faults, _isr_wrapper dispatchers) — the recognition gap is specific to the CMSIS 6 C-template form (typedef'd function-pointer array with cast initial element).

findings.title: lookup_symbol with exact=True silently relaxes to an unrelated-symbol fallback when the name is absent
findings.expected: empty result (documented contract: exact=True = exact name match; the relaxed fallback is documented for prefix/LIKE lookups only)
observed: returns z_impl_k_sleep rows (sched.c + generated syscall headers) with _fallback: True
DB truth (controller oracle): z_impl_printk ABSENT from the index; the relaxation picked a symbol sharing only the z_impl_ token prefix
findings.analysis: the _fallback marker preserves honesty at the row level, but the empty-contract of exact=True is violated: an existence check by an automated caller (non-empty == exists) gets a false positive. Low-medium severity: marked, deterministic, but semantics differ from the documented contract.
